concepts.title: Hot, Cold and Temperature
concepts.definition: Our sense of touch calls iron cold and wool warm, but sense can mislead: temperature is the reliable measure of how hot or cold a body is, read from a thermometer, not felt by the hand.
concepts.key_idea: Feeling deceives, measuring decides: two waters that feel different in each hand may share one temperature.

concepts.title: Thermometers: Clinical and Laboratory
concepts.definition: A thermometer measures temperature with a liquid that expands on heating: clinical thermometers, mercury or digital, are made for body temperature, while laboratory thermometers read a much wider range.
concepts.key_idea: Different jobs, different thermometers: the body's narrow range and the lab's wide range need different scales.

concepts.title: Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin Scales
concepts.definition: Temperature is read on standard scales: the Celsius scale marks water's freezing at 0 and boiling at 100, the Fahrenheit scale reads normal body heat as 98.6 against 37.0 in Celsius, and the SI unit, the kelvin, serves scientific work.
concepts.key_idea: One hotness, several languages: each scale has its own numbers for the same temperature.

concepts.title: Reading a Fever: Rise above Normal
concepts.definition: Normal body temperature of a healthy adult is 37.0 degrees C; a thermometer reading above it signals fever, and the rise, the reading minus the normal value, tells how strong the fever is.
concepts.key_idea: One subtraction turns a thermometer reading into a diagnosis: how far above 37.0 is the fever?
question_patterns: what is the normal body temperature of a healthy adult
how do we know from a reading that a person has fever

solution_steps.explain: Note the body temperature shown by the clinical thermometer.
Normal body temperature is 37.0 degrees C for a healthy adult.
Reading minus normal gives the rise above normal.
